summary: Sacred: 15% of Lemons and Cherries carry Token, 15% of Clovers and Bells carry Ticket, and 15% of Diamonds, Treasures and Sevens are Golden.
tip: Keep it whenever Help! hands it to you: coins, tickets and permanent gem growth from one slot. Gem chance, retriggers and higher Interest all make it better.

synergies.why: Its Repetition on fruit retriggers Token fruit Patterns, paying those Tokens again.
Copy modifiers turn into the nearby Golden, Ticket or Token modifiers, spreading them.
+5% Interest makes every Token pay more.
Ticket modifiers keep your ticket pile, and its Symbols Multiplier, growing.
Every Pattern triggers twice, so every modifier is scored twice.

assumptions: Assumed retriggered Patterns score their modifiers again, as with the store modifier charms.

summary: Sacred: each 999 you score makes every Pattern trigger one extra time for the rest of that Round; several 999s in a Round stack.
tip: Only as good as your 999 rate: Necronomicon, Book of Shadows or Evil Deal raise it, and Possessed Cell Phone can force a 999 on the first spin so the rest of the Round triggers twice.

synergies.why: Forces a 999 on demand; pressed before the first spin, the extra trigger covers the rest of the Round.
Its +3% 666 chance becomes +3% 999 chance in Sacred Mode, plus Patterns Multiplier +2.
Same 999 trigger: extra triggers and a doubled Patterns Multiplier stack for the Round.
The Jackpot that follows a 999 triggers twice, about 20 Patterns.
More 999s, and each one hands out extra spins that get the extra trigger.

antiSynergies.why: A 999 counts as a 666 for charms, so the Bible likely blocks it and wastes the trigger.

assumptions: In Sacred Mode every 666 is a 999, so anything that raises the 666 chance feeds it.
Assumed Holy Bible also cancels 999s, since a 999 counts as a 666 for charms.

summary: Sacred: each 999 you score doubles your Patterns Multiplier until the Round ends; several 999s in one Round multiply (x4, x8...).
tip: Raise your 999 rate (Necronomicon, Evil Deal) or force one early with Possessed Cell Phone so most of the Round is doubled. Stacks with Eternity, which also fires on 999s.

synergies.why: Forces a 999 on demand; early in a Round it doubles almost every spin.
Its +3% 666 chance becomes +3% 999 chance in Sacred Mode: more doubled Rounds.
Doubling the 666 chance doubles the 999 chance in Sacred Mode, so twice as many doubled Rounds.
Same 999 trigger: a doubled multiplier and extra Pattern triggers for the Round.
The Jackpot after a 999 is scored with the doubled multiplier.

antiSynergies.why: A 999 counts as a 666 for charms, so the Bible likely blocks it and wastes the trigger.

assumptions: Encoded as doubling every Pattern's value for the Round, which pays exactly like doubling the Patterns Multiplier (the engine has no Round-long Patterns Multiplier doubling).
Assumed repeated 999s in one Round keep doubling.
Assumed Holy Bible also cancels 999s, since a 999 counts as a 666 for charms.

summary: Sacred: each 999 you score forces a Jackpot on the next spin; extra Jackpots queue up for later spins.
tip: Best with a high 999 rate (Necronomicon, Evil Deal) or Possessed Cell Phone, whose forced 999 becomes a sure Jackpot. I can't quit now! doubles the Jackpot Pattern in each one.

synergies.why: Doubles the Jackpot Pattern's value, the biggest Pattern of every forced Jackpot (about +25% per Jackpot spin).
Every forced Jackpot contains an Eye, so each 999 is followed by an Eye that pays all your 999 coins again.
Each forced 999 becomes a guaranteed Jackpot on the following spin.
With Eternity's extra trigger the Jackpot spin scores about 20 Patterns.
A Jackpot is about 10 Patterns, so it doubles Symbol values for the rest of the Round.
+3% 666 chance means more 999s in Sacred Mode.

antiSynergies.why: A 999 counts as a 666 for charms, so the Bible likely blocks it and wastes the trigger.

assumptions: Assumed the Jackpot lands on the very next spin; the simulator queues only one at a time.
Assumed Holy Bible also cancels 999s, since a 999 counts as a 666 for charms.

summary: Evil: your most likely Symbol(s) get a 20% chance of Revenge; each scored Revenge pays 5% of all coins you have lost to 666 this run.
tip: Useless until a 666 has taken coins; then it turns old losses into steady income. It covers every Symbol tied for most likely (Lemon and Cherry at first); Violence doubles each payout.

effects.text: Revenge: each scored Revenge symbol pays 5% of all coins lost to 666 so far this run, so it pays nothing until a 666 has taken coins.

synergies.why: Revenge pays double: 10% of your 666 losses per scored symbol.
+1 chance for the most likely Symbol, so Sloth's target shows up even more.
Revenge on every Symbol on top, scaling with your 666 chance.

assumptions: Assumed tied Symbols all count as most likely (Lemon and Cherry at base).

summary: Evil, Red Button (1 charge): +10% Interest until the Deadline ends, but your Debt permanently rises by a random 100% to 500%.
tip: Almost always a trap: one press can make every later debt 2-6x bigger for a few rounds of Interest. Store it in a drawer or discard it, especially if you run other Red Button charms.

synergies.why: +10% Interest raises every Cat payout for the rest of the Deadline.

antiSynergies.why: Each press triggers Limbo twice: two debt rises.
Recharges it before every spin and doubles the debt on each press as well.
You press the button for it every Round, and each press also fires a recharged Limbo: another debt rise.

assumptions: The rise is random between +100% and +500% (x2 to x6); encoded as its +300% average.

The debt effect has no Red Button condition on purpose: the engine cannot add debt on a press, and a press presumably fires every charged button charm (Limbo included), so owning it is treated as paying one rise; each further press compounds it.
Assumed the higher debt carries into every later Deadline.

summary: Evil: every Symbol gets +5% chance of Revenge (each scored one pays 5% of your 666 losses this run). Fuses with Lover 2 into Lust.
tip: Too weak to earn a slot alone; keep it in a drawer for the Lust surgery, or use it in a Revenge build next to Violence.

effects.text: Revenge: each scored Revenge symbol pays 5% of all coins lost to 666 so far this run, so it pays nothing until a 666 has taken coins.

synergies.why: Surgery: Lover 1 + Lover 2 fuse into Lust (DLC).
Revenge pays double.
Stacks more Revenge chance on every Symbol.

summary: Evil: +3% chance of 666 and nothing else. Its real use is fusing with Lover 1 into Lust.
tip: Pure downside unless you run 666 payoffs (Baphomet, Gabihbb'h, Revenge charms). Otherwise keep it in a drawer for the Lust surgery or get rid of it.

synergies.why: Surgery: Lover 1 + Lover 2 fuse into Lust (DLC).
Heresy's Revenge chance is double your 666 chance, so +3% adds +6% Revenge.
More 666s, each doubling Above and Below for good.
More 666s make the third one in a Deadline, and its extra Round, likelier.
More 666s, each doubling your Symbols Multiplier for the Round.

antiSynergies.why: Doubles the 666 chance, so this +3% becomes +6%.

summary: Evil: whenever a charm is discarded by an effect (it breaks, decays or a rule removes it), you gain coins equal to everything 666 has taken from you this run.
tip: Pays nothing until a 666 has cost you coins; then every self-breaking charm refunds all of your losses. Fraud or Corpse pieces in drawers, Peppers and Personal Trainer all count.

effects.text: Whenever a charm is discarded by an effect (breaking, decaying to 0, a drawer rule; not selling it from its menu), gain coins equal to the total coins lost to 666 so far this run.

synergies.why: Moving Fraud into a drawer discards it by its own rule: a payout whenever you want it.
Decays to 0% and breaks after 5 Rounds, paying out.
Breaks right after its free Jackpot: a Jackpot plus a payout.
After blocking a 666 it may break, which pays back all your earlier losses.
Brings a broken charm back so it can break, and pay, again.

assumptions: Assumed breaking, decaying to 0% and drawer-discard rules (Fraud, Corpse pieces) all count as discards by an effect; selling does not.
Each payout is the full run total of 666 losses, not only the new ones.

summary: Evil: every Symbol gets a 20% chance of Investor (+1% Interest until the Round ends per scored one), but +2% chance of 666.
tip: Turns busy spins into a climbing Interest rate each Round, so Cats, Tokens and the end-of-Round payout all grow. Deposit early so Interest has coins to work on.

synergies.why: Pays your current Interest on 3+ Pattern spins, and Investor keeps raising it during the Round.
More Investor symbols, and it pays your climbing Interest on every 3+ Pattern spin.
Pays double your climbing Interest on 7+ Pattern spins.
Each Token pays half your current Interest, which Investor pushes up.
Covers the extra 666 risk.

antiSynergies.why: You can only deposit after the last Round, so a higher Interest rate has almost nothing to pay on.

assumptions: Assumed retriggered Patterns score their Investor symbols again.

summary: Evil: when the third 666 of a Deadline shows up, you get one extra Round in that Deadline.
tip: Three 666s in one Deadline are rare unless your 666 chance is near 10%. Lust (two forced 666s every Deadline) or Possessed Cell Phone make it reliable; Heartbreak's forced 666 helps.

effects.text: +1 Round in the current Deadline when the third 666 of that Deadline appears (once per Deadline).

synergies.why: Two guaranteed 666s every Deadline: one more and you get the extra Round.
Order the 666s you need, from Deadline 3 on.
A guaranteed 666 in the last Round of every Deadline.
+1.5% 666 chance, and bonus spins after each 666 give more chances at the next one.
+3% 666 chance.

assumptions: Assumed only the third 666 counts, so at most one extra Round per Deadline.
Kept as text: the engine would value any conditional extra Round as a guaranteed one every Deadline.

summary: Evil: +3% chance of 666, and every Symbol gets a Revenge chance equal to double your total 666 chance (9% with no other 666 boosts).
tip: The engine of a Revenge build: every other 666 boost also raises its Revenge chance. Add Violence for double payouts, and from Deadline 7 deposit often, since a 666 takes all coins you hold.

effects.text: The Revenge chance is always double your current total 666 chance, so it grows with every other 666 boost. Revenge: each scored Revenge symbol pays 5% of all coins lost to 666 so far this run, so it pays nothing until a 666 has taken coins.

synergies.why: Revenge pays double: 10% of your 666 losses per scored symbol.
+3% 666 chance adds +6% Revenge, plus Patterns Multiplier +2.
Doubling the 666 chance also doubles the Revenge chance.
+3% 666 chance adds +6% Revenge.
Its +1.5% 666 chance adds +3% Revenge, and each 666 hands out extra spins.

assumptions: The 0.09 Revenge chance is double the base 1.5% plus Heresy's own 3%; it rises with every other 666 boost.

summary: Evil: every Symbol gets +5% chance of Revenge, and all Revenge modifiers pay double: 10% of your 666 losses this run per scored symbol.
tip: The payoff piece for Revenge charms (Sloth, Heresy, Lover 1, Treachery, Lust). Weak alone; with two or more Revenge sources it turns every past 666 into steady income.

effects.text: All Revenge modifiers, from any source, pay double: 10% of all coins lost to 666 so far this run per scored Revenge symbol.

synergies.why: The biggest Revenge source, and every symbol it marks pays double.
20% Revenge on your most common Symbol, paid double.
30% Revenge on every Symbol in each Deadline's last Round, paid double.
Turns every modifier into Revenge on 40% of spins, all paid double.
More Revenge chance on every Symbol.

summary: Evil: charms in the store cost double, but restocking the store costs half. Moving it into a drawer discards it.
tip: Mostly a tax on buying. Keep it only for a heavy restock phase (Bell Pepper, Electricity Meter), then put it in a drawer to get rid of it; that discard also pays Gluttony.

effects.text: Charm prices in the store are doubled while it is equipped.
Store restocks cost half as many coins while it is equipped.
If you move it into a drawer it is discarded at once (a discard by its own rule).

synergies.why: Putting Fraud in a drawer discards it by an effect, paying Gluttony on demand.
Half-price restocks grow its Luck bonus for fewer coins.
Every half-price restock still recharges a Red Button charm.
Its drawer discard counts as a discard for the Beetle.

antiSynergies.why: Costs 4 tickets instead of 2, so its 4-ticket refund no longer makes a profit.
Every purchase costs twice the tickets, so it grows half as fast per ticket.

assumptions: Assumed the doubling applies after discounts and that free charms stay free.
Assumed the drawer discard counts as a discard by an effect for Gluttony and Dung Beetle.

summary: Evil, triggers randomly (40%): every modifier on the grid turns into Revenge for that spin, replacing Golden, Chain, Repetition and the rest.
tip: Only for pure Revenge builds: with Violence it turns other modifiers into double Revenge payouts. In Golden, Chain or Repetition builds it destroys value on 40% of spins.

effects.text: 40% of spins: every Symbol modifier on the grid becomes Revenge (5% of all coins lost to 666 this run per scored Revenge symbol).

synergies.why: Doubles every Revenge payout it creates.
Its 20% Investor symbols become extra Revenge targets on Treachery spins.
Fires on 80% of spins instead of 40%.

antiSynergies.why: Chain modifiers get converted before they can grow Pattern values.
Repetition modifiers get converted, losing their retriggers.
Golden modifiers get converted, so symbol values grow far slower.

assumptions: Assumed the conversion affects that spin only and only symbols that already carry a modifier.

summary: Cadaver piece a 666 drops in your drawers: equipped, it sits on the slot machine for good and adds +5% Debt; left in the drawer, it is gone at Deadline end.
tip: Equip it only with Skull (a free charm per piece each Deadline) or for the Skeleton Key ending. Otherwise leave it in the drawer: fuse it with Cross into Sacrifice (DLC) or let it vanish.

effects.text: Goes on the slot machine (no charm slot) and can never be discarded once equipped. If it is still in a drawer when a Deadline ends it is discarded. Each equipped Corpse piece makes Skull spawn one free charm per Deadline.

synergies.why: Equipped, it makes Skull spawn one free charm in a drawer every Deadline.
Surgery: this Corpse piece + Cross fuse into Sacrifice (DLC).
If it is discarded from a drawer at the Deadline's end, the Beetle gains a stack.
Left in a drawer, its end-of-Deadline discard pays Gluttony.

summary: Cadaver piece (1 ticket): sits on the slot machine for good, +5% Debt, and each Deadline spawns a free charm in a drawer per Corpse piece you have equipped.
tip: Buy it once you hold Corpse pieces: a Round with a 666 drops one, and charms left in drawers at the end of a run become pieces next run. Four pieces = four free charms every Deadline.

summary: Surgery (any 2 charms), takes no slot: every Symbol permanently gains its base value once.
tip: Turns two spare charms into a permanent boost that is biggest early, while values are low. Skull's free charms or cheap commons make good fodder; each surgery raises the next one's coin cost.

synergies.why: With Corpse pieces it drops free charms into your drawers every Deadline: ready-made fodder.
Charms cost 1 ticket less, so cheap commons become near-free fodder.
Every surgery refunds its coin cost, so repeat fusions are free.
Discarding it returns the charms used in your last surgery, so you can fuse them again.

assumptions: Wiki: ingredients must sit in your drawers and every surgery costs more coins than the last.

summary: Surgery (any 3 charms), takes no slot: Symbols Multiplier +1, permanently.
tip: A clean permanent multiplier for three spare charms, strongest while your Symbols Multiplier is still small. Skull's free charms and Dangerous Experiments make repeat fusions cheap.

tip: Needs all four drawers of fodder but buys a permanent Patterns Multiplier, which few charms give. Repeat it with Skull's free charms; Dangerous Experiments makes the surgeries free.

summary: Surgery (Disc A + B + C): every 2nd spin fires one of Luck +7, forced ZIG and ZAG, or one extra trigger for every Pattern that spin.
tip: All three Disc effects at a faster rate in one slot, freeing two slots. Gets better with large-Pattern value boosts and with charms that reward big spins.

effects.note: One of the three effects fires every 2nd spin, so each fires about 1 spin in 6. Intervals are staggered (5/6/7 spins) so the simulator does not stack all three on the same spin, which never happens in game.
Slightly under the true 1-in-6 rate; Luck (every 5) is slightly over.

synergies.why: Raises ZIG, ZAG and every other 4+ Pattern by its base value.
Doubles every 4+ Symbol Pattern, including the forced ZIG and ZAG.
The forced ZIG and ZAG are 5-symbol Patterns, a sure trigger for the Round.
The forced ZIG and ZAG are 5-symbol Patterns, doubling all Patterns for the Round.
Lucky and retriggered spins push more spins to 5+ Patterns.

assumptions: Assumed one effect fires every 2nd spin, so each averages 1 spin in 6; encoded as Luck every 5, ZIG/ZAG every 6 and retrigger every 7 spins so they never land on the same spin (the old same-spin encoding roughly doubled its value).
Assumed it counts spins across Rounds, like the Discs.

summary: Surgery: 30% of all Symbols carry Copy, which turns into the nearest other modifier on the grid. Drops 1% per Round and breaks at 0% (30 Rounds).
tip: Only as good as your other modifier sources: with Golden, Chain, Repetition or Ticket charms it multiplies how many symbols carry them. Without them on the grid, Copy does nothing.

effects.text: Copy turns into the closest other modifier on the slot machine, so it multiplies whatever Golden, Chain, Repetition, Ticket, Token or Investor modifiers you already roll; with none on the grid it does nothing.

synergies.why: Copies spread its Golden, Ticket and Token modifiers.
Copies spread its Repetition, Battery and Chain modifiers.
Puts modifiers of every kind on the grid for Copy to become, and Amalgama is a Surgery Charm on the table, so it raises Mad Emperor's bonus by 10%.
Copies next to Golden symbols turn Golden too, growing values faster.
Copies next to Ticket symbols pay tickets too.

assumptions: Assumed Copy needs another modified symbol on the grid to copy; the simulator gives Copy no value, so the text effect and ratings carry it.
Wiki: while it is equipped its ingredients (Personal Trainer, Electrician, Fortune Teller) are banned from the store.

summary: Surgery (Red + Green Pepper), triggers randomly (7%): Luck +3 for the rest of the Round. Never breaks.
tip: Weaker than either Pepper it is made from, but permanent and one slot instead of two. Horseshoe doubles its rate, and an early trigger helps more spins.

effects.note: The engine applies the +3 only to the spin that triggers; the real bonus lasts the rest of the Round and stacks (see the special), about 4x the Luck the engine simulates.

effects.text: The Luck +3 lasts for every remaining spin of the Round and stacks if it triggers again.

synergies.why: Doubles its trigger rate to 14%.
Force a trigger on the first spin for Luck +3 on the whole Round.
After a trigger, the Round's last spin gets Luck +7 +3 = 10.

assumptions: Assumed repeated triggers in one Round stack (+3 each).

summary: Surgery (Lucky + Chonky + Swole Cat): 10% of Symbols carry Investor; each 3+ Pattern spin pays your current Interest and adds +5% Investor chance for the Round.
tip: An Interest engine: Investor symbols push Interest up during each Round, so every later payout is bigger. Deposit early in each Deadline and add Stonks or Grandma's Purse.

effects.note: Growing chance (+5% per 3+ Pattern spin, reset each Round): the engine only values the base 10%, so ratings carry the growth.

synergies.why: +5% Interest raises every payout.
+15% Interest for a few Rounds makes each payout much bigger.
+20% Investor chance on every Symbol pushes Interest up faster.
Doubles your Interest, so every payout doubles.
Discard it after the Cat surgery to get all three Cats back as well.

antiSynergies.why: You can only deposit after the last Round, so Interest stays tiny while it pays.

assumptions: Read '+5% until the end of every Round' as +5% Investor chance per 3+ Pattern spin, stacking and resetting each Round.

summary: Surgery (Abyssu + Barathrum + Vorago): when you discard it, every charm used in your last surgery respawns in your drawers, if there is room.
tip: Do your key surgery first, then discard Black Hole to get the ingredients back: keep Cosmic Cat and all three Cats, or re-fuse the fodder for another Dumpster.

effects.text: When discarded, every charm consumed by your most recent surgery respawns in free drawers, so you can keep a fusion and its ingredients, or fuse again.
